detail.summary:
Claim 8841203 (K0001 wheelchair for Marta Reyes) was denied CO-16/N706 for missing documentation. Investigation found the supplier, Lakeshore Home Medical, never actually received the written order/F2F packet because it had been faxed to a closed storefront line (555-0143) that no one monitors. Called Lakeshore, got the correct working documents-line fax number (555-0142), sent the written order and F2F note there, Lakeshore confirmed receipt and resubmitted the claim, which then paid in full ($249.60 paid, $62.40 patient responsibility).

Why resolve (not escalate): The claim was denied for missing documentation because the original fax went to a defunct storefront number; Lakeshore confirmed they never received the order/F2F note. After confirming the correct documents-line number via call:1, I faxed the written order and F2F note there, Lakeshore confirmed receipt (inbox:348) and resubmitted, and the claim is now FINALIZED — PAID (inbox:349), proving the blocker is genuinely resolved.

Why resolve (not escalate): The original denial (CO-27, coverage terminated) was correct: Harold's Original Medicare Part B terminated 12/31 when he enrolled in Humana Gold Plus MA effective 1/1, confirmed by the Medicare provider line and Humana provider services. The supplier (ChicagoLand Durable Medical) was reached, given the correct Humana payer ID/member ID, and rebilled the claim under new claim number 9004117 to Humana, which now shows ACCEPTED — IN PROCESS, proving the claim is being paid correctly by the party that actually covered the DOS.

Goal: get Ana Kowalski's manual wheelchair (K0001, written order signed day -24 by Dr. M. Sandoval) delivered to 1622 S Ridgeland Ave, Berwyn, IL 60402.

What I found: The prior advocate's day -9 call to Prairie State got a verbal promise of Thursday/Friday delivery; nothing arrived (confirmed via texts with Ana on day -4 and day -1: "No nothing came... Still nothing"). 

My attempts to re-engage Prairie State (day 0 onward):
- Called directory primary number (773) 555-0211: disconnected/out of service (call:1).
- Called directory alt number (773) 555-0212: rang out, mailbox full, cannot leave message (call:2).
- Sent a fax to Prairie State (fax-sent:1) with the written order and an urgent request to confirm status or reship — no reply after advancing the clock through day 42, 45, 50, and 57 (57 days total, 4 advances, nothing landed — inbox check confirmed only Ana's text, no supplier reply).
- Re-tried the primary phone number on day 50: same disconnected message (call:3).
- Texted Ana to check if she'd heard anything independently; she has not, and confirmed she's home most days and just needs a call-ahead (inbox:354).

Conclusion: Prairie State appears to be defunct or otherwise non-functional as a business — disconnected main line, full voicemail on the alt line, and no response whatsoever to a faxed follow-up over nearly two months. There is no channel left that reaches this supplier.

I do not have the practice's identity/contact confirmed in this case file (only the prescriber's name, no clinic listed), so I could not independently pursue the re-order path — this needs a human to confirm which practice Dr. Sandoval belongs to and authorize redirection.

Ana is waiting, home most days, no wheelchair yet. No claim was ever filed (claim_ids empty), so this is purely a fulfillment/delivery blocker, not a billing/denial issue.

detail.package:
Goal: schedule Eleanor Martinez's wheelchair (K0001, order signed day -19 by Dr. Okafor) for delivery via Lakeshore Home Medical.

Timeline/facts gathered:
- Patient has been hospitalized at Rush since day -6 (heart-related), per her daughter/emergency contact Rosa Martinez, with no discharge date given and mention of a probable rehab stay afterward "two weeks, maybe more."
- Patient's phone is sitting unused at home; texting her is pointless (confirmed by Rosa, and by 4 prior unanswered texts before I took the case).
- Lakeshore Home Medical had the wheelchair ready to dispatch but only holds stock 30 days; I called them and confirmed (call:2) the hold expired on day 19 and the unit has gone back to stock. They stated: "if she still needs it you're starting the order over. New delivery date once we have a window from her."
- I called Rosa twice (call:1, call:3) — both times reached her, no new information; she says she will call back once Eleanor is home, and asked not to keep contacting Eleanor's phone.
- I advanced time repeatedly (through day 73, ~94 days since hospitalization began) with no inbound reply from Rosa, Eleanor, or any other channel.

Current blocker: This is not a documentation/billing/payer issue — the written order (doc:written-order) is valid and there's no claim yet to fix. The blocker is purely that the patient is incapacitated/hospitalized long-term and unreachable, and the dispensed unit already lapsed back to supplier stock. Nothing in my available channels (texting patient, calling daughter, calling supplier) can produce a delivery window because the patient herself must provide it, and she is medically unable to.

What's needed next: A human should periodically check with Rosa (or facility) for Eleanor's actual discharge date, then contact Lakeshore Home Medical to re-open/re-issue the order (since the original stock hold expired) and schedule delivery once Eleanor is home and able to receive equipment. No further automated action can move this — it depends on real-world medical recovery timeline outside this system's tools.

Evidence ids: call:1, call:2, call:3, doc:supplier-hold, doc:written-order

Why escalate (not resolve): The blocker is a real-world medical/logistics gap (patient hospitalized indefinitely, phone unused, stock hold expired) that cannot be resolved through calls, texts, or faxes — it requires a human to monitor for Eleanor's actual discharge over an indefinite period and then re-engage the supplier, which is outside what repeated automated outreach can accomplish.

detail.reason: Referral to cardiology expired and PCP practice has not issued a renewal/redirect despite repeated follow-up over ~4 months; patient still has not been seen for urgent post-afib cardiology follow-up.
detail.package:
Patient: Grace Adeyemi, 70, Original Medicare Part B. Goal: get her seen by cardiology after an ED visit for new-onset afib with RVR (ED discharge, day -5, recommended cardiology follow-up within 30 days per case file).

Blocker: The original referral to Lakefront Cardiology Associates (from Dr. Whitfield, Evanston Primary Care) expired on day +28. Lakefront's scheduling office confirmed by phone (call:1, call:2) that they cannot book any appointment without a current, valid referral on file, and their next opening is weeks out regardless. I faxed Lakefront asking them to re-verify the referral (fax-sent:1) — no reply after multiple advances of time.

I then called Evanston Primary Care (Dr. Whitfield's office) to get the referral renewed or redirected. Front desk stated (call:3, call:4, call:5, call:6 — identical each time) that only Dr. Whitfield can approve a renewal or redirect, that he reviews these in batches, typically ~2 weeks, and that he might require Grace to be seen in-office again first before deciding. I faxed the ED discharge summary and referral to expedite (fax-sent:2). On day 104 a fax reply confirmed the request was received and "placed in Dr. Whitfield's review queue. No determination at this time" (inbox:356). Despite waiting through day 122 (well beyond the quoted ~2-week turnaround, and repeated follow-up calls all returning the same canned front-desk response with no new status), no determination has been issued.

Patient contact: Grace confirmed by text (inbox:357) she is willing to travel and her son can drive her on Saturdays, so scheduling logistics are not the obstacle — the paperwork is.

What's unresolved: Dr. Whitfield has not signed off on a referral renewal or redirect. Without that, Lakefront (or any other cardiology practice) will not schedule her. This is now a ~4-month delay against a 30-day recommended follow-up window for new-onset afib with RVR, which is clinically concerning.

Hypotheses:
1. Dr. Whitfield's office is simply backlogged/unresponsive beyond their own stated SLA — needs a human to press harder (e.g., escalate within the practice, or file a complaint) or physically get Grace an office visit if that's what's required to trigger sign-off.
2. Practice may be understaffed/dysfunctional — worth considering redirecting to a different practice, or exploring whether Lakefront would accept an urgent verbal/interim referral given the ED records, bypassing the normal batch queue.

Recommended next step: A human advocate should either (a) push Dr. Whitfield's office through a supervisor/patient-advocate escalation path to force a determination given the clinical urgency, (b) schedule Grace for an in-person visit with Dr. Whitfield if that's what he needs to sign off, or (c) contact Lakefront's office manager directly (not just scheduling) to ask whether they would accept an expedited/urgent referral given the ED records showing new-onset afib with RVR.

Evidence ids: call:1, call:2, call:3, call:4, call:5, call:6, fax-sent:1, fax-sent:2, inbox:356, inbox:357, doc:referral

Why escalate (not resolve): The blocker (Dr. Whitfield's sign-off on a referral renewal/redirect) requires clinical judgment and practice-internal escalation that is outside my available channels (phone/fax/text); repeated calls and a fax yielded only a queued, undetermined status for weeks past the practice's own stated SLA, so a human needs to intervene directly with the practice or arrange an in-person visit.
